lead: The Rules are asked here by number and paragraph, for a yacht of 20 m or more, where the small-craft allowances stop: which rule governs, what it asks, and who the other vessel is.

blocks.p: **Under way** (3(i)): not at anchor, made fast or aground, so on a sea anchor you are under way. **Not under command** (3(f)) needs an exceptional circumstance; dismasted but motoring: power-driven. **In sight** (3(k)): by eye only.

Rule 5: a look-out by sight and hearing, always. Rule 6: radar's limits count against speed. Rule 7 says when risk exists, Rule 8 how to act; taking way off (8(e)) clears one vessel when a turn would close another. A plot gives her true course, hence the rule. Rule 2 adds seamanship: call her, light your sails.

fig.note: Her bridge bears aft; her bow, 300 m ahead, may not

fig.title: Risk and action (Rules 7 and 8)
lines: Steady compass bearing, or doubt: risk
After your own turn a relative bearing lies
A minute of radar data is scanty (7(c))
Huge ship close: risk even as bearing moves
Early, one large obvious alteration (8(b))
Hold on until finally past and clear (8(d))

blocks.p: Keep to the starboard side of a channel (9(a)). Under 20 m or sailing, do not impede a vessel confined to it (9(b)); at 20 m under power you meet her under Rule 14. Fishing impedes nobody there (9(c)); nobody crosses if that impedes a channel-bound vessel (9(d)). **Not to impede** means leaving room early; once risk exists both duties stand (8(f)).

fig.note: Follow the lane, or cross it at right angles

fig.title: Rule 10 at a glance
lines: (b) Follow the lane; join at a small angle
(c) Cross on a heading at right angles
(d) Inshore zone: <20 m, sail, fishing, or
bound for a port inside it
(e) Separation zone: emergency, or fishing
(g) No anchoring · (h) unused: keep clear

blocks.p: Rule 10 relieves nobody of the other rules (a): at 20 m under power Rules 13 and 15 apply as anywhere; under 20 m or sailing you also must not impede ships following the lane (j). All but NUC and RAM avoid impeding a vessel **constrained by her draught** (18(d)); a cable ship at work is exempt (l).

**Overtaking** (13): from more than 22.5° abaft her beam, where only her sternlight shows. It overrides the rest, whatever she is: keep clear until past and clear; a later bearing change changes nothing. **Head-on** (14): both to starboard, boldly; in doubt assume it. **Crossing** (15): the one with the other on her starboard side keeps clear. Port tack, a windward yacht's tack unknown: keep clear (12(a)(iii)).

fig.note: Abaft her beam (120° from her bow): overtaking

fig.title: Rule 17: the stand-on vessel
lines: (a)(i) Keep your course and speed
(a)(ii) May act once she plainly does not
(b) Must act when she alone cannot avoid it
(c) Power: no turn to port for one to port
A VHF agreement overrides none of this

blocks.p: Rule 18: power yields to sail, both to fishing, all to RAM and NUC. A warship recovering aircraft is RAM; a pilot vessel plain power. Seaplanes and WIG craft keep clear of all; a seaplane on the water follows the steering rules once risk exists.

Rule 19 governs vessels **not in sight** of one another in or near restricted visibility, radar and VHF contact or not. Act in ample time, avoiding a turn to port for a vessel forward of the beam, unless overtaking her, and a turn towards one abeam or abaft it (19(d)). If neither is open, or a fog signal sounds forward of the beam, slow to bare steerage way or stop (19(e)). Ten degrees barely moves the CPA.

fig.note: Fog · overtaking her: a turn to port is allowed

fig.title: Fog signals (Rule 35)
lines: Power, making way: 1 prolonged, every 2 min
Power, under way, stopped: 2 prolonged
NUC/RAM/sail/fishing/tow: 1 long, 2 short
At anchor: bell 5 s/min; 100 m+: gong aft
Aground: 3 strokes, the bell, 3 strokes

blocks.p: A pushing unit sounds as one. From 20 m you carry and ring a bell; at anchor add short, prolonged, short to warn a vessel standing into you.

Masthead light 225°, each sidelight 112.5°, sternlight and yellow towing light the other 135°: her lights fix her aspect. Masthead lights and red: you are forward of her port beam; yellow over white: in her stern arc.

fig.note: 40° on her port bow: masthead lights and red

blocks.p: From 20 m a sailing yacht loses the tricolour (25(b)): separate sidelights and sternlight, red over green optional at the masthead, never with the engine driving; seen with a steaming light, assume the worse. Under sail, no masthead light: a ship sees her at two miles. Under 50 m a second masthead light is optional.

fig.title: Rule 22 and Annex I, from 20 m
lines: Masthead 5 M (3 M under 20 m); the rest 2 M
Masthead ≥ 6 m up, or her breadth if more
Sidelights no higher than ¾ of it
Vertical line: 2 m apart, the lowest 4 m up
2nd masthead: 4.5 m higher, half length aft
Manoeuvring light: 5 M, 2 m from masthead

fig.note: Shapes from 20 m: a ball at least 0.6 m across

blocks.p: **Towing** (24): two masthead lights in a line, three when the tow, tug's stern to its end, exceeds 200 m (a diamond by day); yellow towing light over the sternlight, so from astern the length is hidden. A rigid pushing unit is one power vessel. Towing your tender, you show them; 24(i) relieves only a tow in distress. A long, low tow: whites at each end and every 100 m.

**NUC** (27(a)): two reds, two balls; sidelights and sternlight only when making way through the water, not drifting. **RAM**: red, white, red; ball, diamond, ball; at anchor plus anchor light. A dredger: two reds on the blocked side, two greens to pass; at anchor these replace anchor lights. A small dive boat: red, white, red, or a rigid flag A, 1 m. Three greens or balls in a triangle: mine clearance. **Aground**: anchor light and two reds; three balls.

fig.title: Annex II: trawlers working together
lines: Shooting nets: two whites below
Hauling: white over red
Net fast on an obstruction: two reds
Pair trawlers (searchlights): never between
Purse seiner hampered: two yellows flashing

blocks.p: Manoeuvring signals (34(a)) belong to a **power-driven** vessel under way, in sight of another: one short blast, to starboard; two, to port; three, engines astern. Under sail, none. A light may repeat them (34(b)): an all-round white seen at 5 M, 2 m from the masthead light, one flash per blast.

fig.note: One flash: I am altering my course to starboard

blocks.p: Annex III, from 20 m: a whistle of 250–700 Hz heard at 1 M (a 200 m ship: 2 M), a bell with a 300 mm mouth. To attract attention (36): any signal not mistakable for another, a searchlight on your sails, never her bridge. **Annex IV** lists the distress signals; any use except in distress is forbidden.

fig.title: Annex IV: distress
lines: A gun or explosion about once a minute
A fog signal sounded continuously; SOS
Flames aboard; red flares; orange smoke
Square flag + ball; arms slowly up and down
MAYDAY, DSC, EPIRB · not an inverted ensign
Orange sheet (square, circle): for aircraft
